source_text: 1. S: autem hee illorum umbram dicent esse, quemadmodum quidam ipsorum audent dicere, ut secundum hoc imagines esse, necesse erit et corpora ipsos ea quz sunt sursum confiteri. Ea enim qu sursum sunt corpora umbram faciunt, non autem jam spiritalia, quandoquidem nulli obscurare possunt. Si autem et demus illis hoc, quod quidem est impossibile, eorum qure sunt spiritala et lucida umbram esse, in quam Matrem suam descendisse dicunt, tamen cum illa sint zeterna, et ea que ex ipsis efficitur umbra sempiterna perseverat, et non jam transeunt hzc, sed perseverant cum his, que se adumbrant. Si autem hzc transeunt, et illa necesse est, quorum hzc sunt umbra, transire : illis autem perseverantibus, perseverat et umbra ipsorum. Si autem non secundum id quod obumbretur, dicent eam umbram esse, sed secundum id quod multo ab illis separata sint, paterni luminis ipsorum pusillitatem et infirmitatem accusabunt, quasi non attingat usque ad hzc, sed deficiat adimplere id quod est vacuum, et dissolvere umbram, et hoc quando nemo sit impedimento. In caliginem enim convertetur secundum eos et obceecabitur paternum lumen eorum, et deficiet in his quee sunt vacuitatis locis, cum minime possit adimplere omnia. 2. Non igitur jam dicant Pleroma esse omnium Bythum ipsorum ; siquidem id quod est vacuum et umbra neque adimplevit neque illuminavit: aut iterum umbram et vacuum pretermittant, siquidem adimplet omnia paternum ipsorum lumen. Neque igitur extra prinum Patrem, id est qui super omnia est Deus, aut Pleroma aliquid esse potest, in quod Enthymesin passi /Eonis descendisse dicunt, ut non definiatur et circumscribatur ab eo qui est extra, et contineatur ipsum Pleroma, vel primus Deus : neque vacuum esse, aut umbram capiet, cum jam ante sit Pater, uti ne deficiat lumen ejus, et definiatur in vacuum. Irrationale est autem et impium adinvenire locum, in quo cessat et finem habet qui est secundum eos Propator et Proarche, et omnium Pater et hujus Pleromatis. Nec rursus in Patris sinu alterum quendam dicere tantam fabricasse conditionem fas est, vel consentiente, vel non consentiente eo, propter preedictas causas. Impium est enim similiter et demens dicere, tantam conditionem ab angelis, aut ab emissione quadam ignorante verum Deum, in his quz sunt ipsius, fabricasse: neque intra Pleroma ipsorum, cum sit universum spiritale, ea quee sunt terrena et choica possibile facta esse: sed ne quidem secundum illorum imaginem, cum dicuntur pauci et similis formationis et unum esse, possibile est et quze sunt multz conditionis et contraria invicem facta esse. 3. Falsus autem apparuit, et qui est de umbra cenomatis, id est vacui, ipsorum sermo secundum omnia. Itaque vacuum ostensum est figmentum eorum, et inconstans doctrina: vacui autem et hi qui attendunt eis, vere in profundum perditionis descendentes.
thought_title: Refutation of Heretical Views on the Pleroma
pass_a_gloss: But they will say that this is the shadow of those things, just as some of them dare to say, so that according to this, images must exist, and it is necessary that they also confess that the bodies themselves, which are above, are those things. For the bodies which are above make a shadow, but not spiritual things, since they cannot obscure anything. But if we also grant them this, which is impossible, that spiritual and luminous things have a shadow, into which they say their Mother descended, nevertheless, since those things are eternal, and the shadow which is made from them is perpetual, it perseveres and does not pass away, but perseveres with those things which are shadowed. But if these things pass away, it is necessary that those things, of which these are shadows, also pass away; but with those things persevering, their shadow also perseveres. But if they say that it is a shadow, not according to what is shadowed, but according to what is much separated from them, they will accuse the smallness and weakness of their paternal light, as if it does not reach up to these things, but fails to fill what is empty, and to dissolve the shadow, and this when there is no one hindering. For according to them, the paternal light of theirs will be converted into darkness and will be obscured, and will fail in those places which are of emptiness, when it is least able to fill all things. Therefore, they should not say that the Pleroma is the Bythos of all their things; for what is empty and a shadow, neither fills nor illuminates; or again, they should neglect the shadow and the empty, since the paternal light of theirs fills all things. Nor can the Pleroma, or the first God, who is above all things, be outside the first Father, that is, God, into which they say the Enthymesin of the /Eonis descended, so that it is not defined and circumscribed by what is outside, and the Pleroma itself is contained, or the first God; nor can it be empty, or take on a shadow, since the Father already exists, so that his light does not fail, and is defined in the empty. It is irrational and impious to invent a place in which what is, according to them, the Propator and Proarche, and the Father of all, and of this Pleroma, ceases and has an end. Nor is it right to say that in the Father's bosom, another certain one has fabricated such a condition, either with his consent or without his consent, for the aforementioned reasons. It is impious and foolish to say that such a condition has been fabricated by angels, or by some ignorant emission of the true God, in those things which are his; nor can those things which are earthly and choic be made within their Pleroma, since it is a spiritual universe; nor is it possible, according to their image, since they say that a few and similar formations are one, that those things which are of many conditions and contrary to each other can be made. But their speech, which is from the shadow of the empty, that is, of their vacuum, has appeared false according to all things. Thus, the empty has been shown to be their fiction, and their doctrine is inconstant; and those who attend to them are truly descending into the depths of perdition.

pass_b_english: They will claim that this is the shadow of those realities, just as some among them dare to assert, so that, according to this logic, images must exist. It then becomes necessary for them to confess that the bodies themselves which are above are those very things. Bodies that are above cast a shadow, but spiritual things do not, since they cannot obscure anything. Even if we granted them this impossible concession—that spiritual and luminous things have a shadow, into which they say their Mother descended—the consequence remains: since those things are eternal, the shadow produced from them is perpetual. It endures and does not pass away, but perseveres together with the things that cast it. If, however, those shadows pass away, then the realities of which they are shadows must also pass away; but if the realities persevere, their shadow perseveres with them. If they say it is a shadow not according to what is overshadowed, but according to what is widely separated from them, they will accuse the smallness and weakness of their paternal light, as though it does not reach these realms but fails to fill what is empty and to dissolve the shadow—and this when no one stands in the way. According to them, their paternal light would be converted into darkness and be obscured; it would fail in those places of emptiness, since it is least able to fill all things.

Therefore they should no longer say that the Pleroma is the Bythos of all their realities; for what is empty and a shadow neither fills nor illuminates. Or else they should dismiss the shadow and the empty altogether, since their paternal light fills all things. Neither can the Pleroma, nor the first God who is above all, exist outside the first Father—that is, the God who is over all—into which they say the Enthymesis of the Aeons descended, so that it might not be defined and circumscribed by what is outside, and so that the Pleroma itself might be contained, or the first God. Nor can it be empty or receive a shadow, since the Father already exists, lest his light fail and be defined within emptiness. It is irrational and impious to invent a place where, according to them, the Propator and Proarche, the Father of all and of this Pleroma, ceases and has an end. Nor is it permissible to say that within the Father's bosom another being fabricated such a condition, whether with his consent or without it, for the reasons already stated. It is equally impious and foolish to claim that such a condition was fabricated by angels, or by some ignorant emission of the true God, within the realms that belong to him. Nor can those things which are earthly and base be brought into existence within their Pleroma, since it is a wholly spiritual universe. Nor is it possible even according to their own image: since they say that a few, similar formations are one, it cannot follow that things of many conditions and contrary to one another could be produced.

Their word, which comes from the shadow of the void—that is, of their vacuum—has proved false in every respect. Thus the void has been exposed as their fiction, and their doctrine as inconstant; and those who give heed to them are truly descending into the depths of perdition.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent English version that preserves all nuances, including the technical Gnostic terms (Pleroma, Bythos, Enthymesis, Propator, Proarche) and the complex conditional arguments regarding the nature of shadows and the paternal light.
